niche: a foundation's volatility-premium sleeve selling S&P 500 variance swaps on a monthly ladder: how large a second, 3-month ladder can run beside the 12-month one inside a settlement-loss limit and a collateral limit measured on the record since January 2007, when the Cboe download of the 3-month volatility index begins in September 2009, with every open swap marked at accrued plus implied variance for its remaining term under the cap; how firmly the record pins each ladder's average settlement when sales a month apart overlap; and the 2027 plan over every settlement that falls in the year, with its range
analyst_test: A careful analyst who applies every filed rule, marks swaps at the implied variance for their remaining terms under the cap, runs both ladders through the record and replays the open swaps jointly still files about USD 124,500 a point and a plan of about USD 5.56m with ranges that are too narrow, because the missing 3-month strikes are stood in for by a regression on the 30-day index that fits the whole overlap and is 2.3 points high on its stressed days, the open swaps are planned at their value, which the record shows to understate what such swaps go on to pay, and settlements are resampled one at a time although neighbouring sales share most of their days
domain_test: Sizing a variance-swap ladder against settlement and collateral limits is volatility-derivatives work end to end: strikes read from the implied term structure, realised variance accrued from closes, seasoned swaps marked at accrued plus implied variance for the remaining term under the cap, expected settlement set apart from the mark by what the record shows realised variance to be against implied, and inference corrected for overlapping settlements; swap the swaps for hospital beds and there is no strike, no accrued variance, no term structure that inverts in a crisis, no overlap between one month's sale and the next and no mark to tell from an expectation

driver: The decisive quantity is how large a new recurring commitment can run beside an existing one inside two limits measured on a long published record, when the file of the price series the new commitment is struck on begins after the record's worst episode: its missing early levels are rebuilt from the neighbouring series on both sides, because its relation to the nearer one reverses in stress and a one-series stand-in passes a check on the whole overlap; the room on the binding day comes from valuing every open commitment at the quoted level for its remaining life; next year's receipts from the commitments already open are their expectation on the record's realised outcomes against quoted ones, which the day's valuation understates; and because commitments made a month apart share most of their life, an average's range and the year's range have to keep neighbouring ones together
driver_concrete: A 3-month variance-swap ladder beside the USD 50,000-a-point 12-month ladder fits both limits up to USD 114,400 a point (collateral on 20 November 2008): the 3-month index file starts on 18 September 2009, its 2007 to 2009 strikes are rebuilt from the 30-day and the 6-month or 1-year indices (it sits 12 per cent above the 30-day index on average and 8 per cent below it when that index is over 35), every open swap is marked at accrued plus implied variance for its remaining term under the 2.5 times cap, the ten open sale months that expire in 2027 are expected to settle at about USD 2.5m against a value of USD 1.9m, the 12-month ladder's average of USD 315,000 per USD 100,000 a point is pinned only to 63,000 to 552,000 four times in five, and the 2027 plan over all 21 settlements is USD 5.7m with a range from a payment of 4.2m to receipts of 12.2m
stump: A competent solver stands the 30-day index in for the missing 3-month strikes by a regression that explains 0.94 of the index where both are published, plans the open swaps at their value and resamples settlements one at a time, filing about USD 124,500 a point, a plan of 5.56m and ranges of 228,000 to 400,000 for the 12-month average; one who leaves the early sale dates out files 136,600; swaps valued at their own index give 144,400, the new ladder sized on its own 184,100, no cap in the valuation 38,900, a forecast made in volatility and squared a plan of 6.25m, against USD 114,400 a point and 5.73m with a range of minus 4.2m to 12.2m
results: R1 the 3-month ladder's average settlement per sale on the record since 2007, its early strikes rebuilt; R2 its worst calendar year; R3 the 12-month ladder's peak collateral on the record; R4 the largest 3-month size inside both limits beside the 12-month ladder, with the limit and day that bind; R5 the largest 6-month size instead; R6 the 80 per cent range of the 12-month ladder's average settlement per sale; R7 the same for the 3-month ladder; R8 the expected 2027 settlement of the open swaps; R9 its 80 per cent range; R10 the 2027 plan by ladder over every settlement that falls in the year, with its range; R11 the recommendation
one_fact_test: the most useful single sentence ('on the days that set the limit the 3-month index sits below the 30-day index, so the missing strikes have to come from the maturities on both sides of three months') rescues R1, R2 and R4, 3 of 11; 'an open swap's value is a price: expect what such swaps went on to pay on the record' rescues R8, 1 of 11; 'keep neighbouring sales together when the record is resampled' rescues R6, 1 of 11; two moves at once rescue 4, 5 and 2 of 11 and the plan and the recommendation need all three; all are method choices on public data used as is, nothing is hidden or built in

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a tail probability of a sum of losses, each a default times a severity, where the severity falls in the very states that cluster the defaults, through the same latent shock of the shared owner, a state of the owner's whole book; a severity averaged over the record prices the tail at the average state, one tied to the economy alone misses the owner's shock, one read off the co-defaults inside the portfolio prices a thin slice of an owner as isolated failures, and only the severity conditioned on each owner-year's shock, inferred from that owner-year's default experience across its book, carries the tail.

notes: stump_strategy other: three beyond-reflex judgments on public data: a frame the index file leaves out, rebuilt with a method that holds in stress where a one-index stand-in passes a whole-overlap check; a real-world expectation set against a risk-neutral value; and inference on overlapping settlements. population_selection would be the nearest key for the first and was in the ban window at the draw. gate_g forecasting: the call is next year's ladder and plan, which the record read correctly does not pin without the rebuild, the real-world premium and the dependence between neighbouring sales. Positions and paperwork are authored; every market value is public and unaltered. The 3-month index's earlier published closes (FRED, from December 2007) are a cross-check held outside the pack, and every band holds the answers they give.
